title: Cross-border lockstep onboarding notes and grace-period playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the operator and solutions teams describing a lockstep onboarding approach when we start enforcing region pins (aka "territorial pins") for customers. The emphasis here is on handling grace periods and retention adjustments so customers are not unexpectedly disrupted while we bring enforcement live.

Context and motivation:
- We are moving from advisory region assignment -> automated regional enforcement (phase gated).
- Key risk: customers with cross-border historical KV/objects will have in-flight state that needs to be reconciled or expired before enforcement to avoid service outages.
- We need a clear, operator-friendly playbook for: grace period windows, eviction/replication timelines, legal-hold exceptions, and telemetry tags that identify affected tenants.

Definitions (operational):
- Lockstep onboarding: progressively enabling enforcement for a cohort of customers while maintaining service continuity via temporary grace windows and targeted migrations.
- Grace window: a customer-specific period (0-90 days) during which cross-border requests are allowed but are recorded and rate-limited.
- Eviction window: period after grace window end during which tokens/keys originating outside pinned region are systematically expired (with notices).
- Soft-fail: return 409 + helpful diagnostic placeholder to app instead of hard 500 for region mismatch.

High-level policy proposal (staging -> prod):
1) Preflight (observability + comms): run a 30-day telemetry sweep to classify tenants by: % cross-border traffic, last-write timestamp outside anchored region, number of assets > threshold. Create "residency-risk" tag.
2) Opt-in pilot: invite low-risk customers to enforcement pilot with a 60-day grace period. During pilot, we allow cross-border reads but block writes after 45 days unless migration started.
3) Lockstep cohorts: enforce in cohorts based on risk bands. Typical timeline per cohort:
   - Day 0: cohort selected and notification sent (email + console banner).
   - Day 7: diagnostic snapshot delivered and runbook created (operator + customer).
   - Day 30: enforcement toggles to soft-fail mode; return structured errors and guidance UX.
   - Day 60: eviction window begins (per-customer TTL applied to cross-border cached prefixes).
   - Day 90: hard enforcement (requests routed/blocked according to pin).

Grace-period mechanics (implementation notes):
- Customer-level config: grace_period_days (int), allowed_origin_tags (list), legal_hold (bool). Default: 60 days for standard customers; 90 for enterprise with contract clause.
- System behavior while grace_period active:
  * Writes originating outside the pinned region are accepted but recorded with header X-Residency-Flag:grace and stored in a temporary append-only journal that is geographically annotated.
  * Reads prefer local anchors but will fall back to nearest replica.
  * KV/Prefix caching: mark entries with cross_border=true and schedule prioritized replication if customer initiated a migration.
- Eviction semantics: after grace expiry, for non-migrated keys mark as stale and set per-key TTL (default 14 days) then expire. For stateful objects we attempt required replication then eviction; if replication fails, move to legal-hold queue and alert SLA owner.

Customer comms templates (operator notes):
- 30-day notice: "We will begin enforcing region pins for your tenant on <date>. For 60 days you will be in a grace period where cross-region writes are accepted and logged. Please see the diagnostic report attached and contact your solutions engineer to schedule migration steps."
- Soft-fail message (API surface): 409 {"code":"RESIDENCY_SOFT_FAIL","message":"Write would violate region pin. Grace period active. See console for migration steps.","help_link":"<url>"}

Telemetry & instrumentation (must-haves):
- tenant.residency.risk (enum: low|medium|high) 
- tenant.residency.cross_border_write_pct (float) 
- tenant.residency.last_out_of_region_write (timestamp)
- operator.alerts: resid-eviction-failures, legal-hold-created, migration-initiated
- expose a console table with filters for "grace_period_expires_within_30d" and "pending_legal_holds"

Operator runbook (day-by-day checklist for a cohort):
- Day -14: run telemetry sweep, prepare cohort list, send legal + sales heads summary.
- Day -7: open runbook ticket (JIRA) with migration owner assigned. Insert link to diagnostic artifact.
- Day 0: toggle cohort flag in staging, enable verbose logging. Inform oncall.
- Day 7: check for migration plan; if none, schedule immediate customer outreach.
- Day 30: verify soft-fail metrics (error rate, customer support tickets). If error rate > 2% escalate to SRE lead.
- Day 60: start eviction; run small canary eviction (5 tenants) and verify data durability and logs.
- Day 90: flip enforcement flag; monitor traffic and rollback plan available for 72h.

Rollback & rollback criteria:
- Immediate rollback if any of: data loss > 0.01% of items for cohort, customer reports inability to perform critical writes > 5 minutes, or systemic replication errors observed.
- Rollback mechanics: flip enforcement flag off for cohort, rehydrate keys from append-only journals (if present), open incident and assign priority P0.

Legal holds and exceptions:
- Legal-hold API: allow _legal_hold=true on tenant metadata; legal_hold bypasses default eviction but still records events. Legal team must sign off for permanent exemptions.
- Exemptions lifecycle: create docs with timeboxed expansion - typical max 180 days unless legal escalates. Track in "residency-exemptions" spreadsheet (link in linked_artifacts).

Open engineering questions / TODOs:
- How to surface per-tenant journal size and growth control? Need an SLO to limit disk usage per tenant during grace.
- Can we provide a zero-downtime grafting utility that re-parents KV prefixes into local anchors without requiring re-write by the app? (proto idea: prefix-level rekey + tombstone + replay)
- How to represent partial migrations in telemetry and billing? We should avoid charging cross-region egress during grace for existing customers — finance needs a short calc doc.
- Operational cost estimate: sample cohort of 500 mid-size tenants expected to add ~12% extra replication traffic during grace; need capacity planning for next two quarters.

Notes to self / meeting prompts for next sync with solutions-eng (scheduled 2024-11-18):
- Bring concrete replication cost numbers from infra (Noah).
- Draft message templates for sales/legal to use for enterprise exceptions (Priya).
- Validate JIRA flow (Liam) and create accelerator scripts for runbook steps.

Appendix: quick scripts and sample API flags (copyable)
- Toggle cohort: PATCH /admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/residency {"enforcement_cohort":"cohort-2025-01"} 
- Set grace-window: PATCH /admin/tenants/{tenant_id} {"grace_period_days":60} 
- Query diagnostic: GET /admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/residency-diagnostics -> returns cross_border_pct, last_out_of_region_write

End of note.

-- Maya
(working draft; will convert to formal runbook after pilot)
